_note: Batch 13 — retail & restaurants (the PE debt-load-and-die pattern). Retrospective/cautionary batch: 4 of 5 are ownership_status=former (liquidated or exited); Sears is confirmed (ESL still controls the Transformco remnant). Imported via import-to-airtable.mjs; businesses land review_status=pending, evidence lands publish=true but still needs the publish checkbox verified. All evidence is Tier B (bankruptcy filings, reporting, and private litigation — not government enforcement) and tagged Financial extraction, illustrating the leveraged-buyout mechanism (debt loading, dividend recaps, sale-leasebacks). Cross-links: Bain Capital (also iHeart) and Leonard Green (also Wrench + Aspen) already exist as firms with no firm tags, so no bleed. Toys R Us is placed under Bain (a co-lead with KKR + Vornado) specifically to avoid KKR's PetVet firm-tag bleeding onto it.

firms.notes: Eddie Lampert's hedge fund; controlled Sears Holdings from the 2005 Kmart merger through its 2018 bankruptcy, and now the ESL-controlled remnant, Transformco.
Bought Red Lobster from Darden in 2014 (and formerly owned Payless ShoeSource, Eddie Bauer and others).
Retail-focused PE firm; portfolio has included Nine West, Aeropostale, Staples, Belk and Talbots.

businesses.platform_company: Iconic toy retailer; taken private in a 2005 $6.6B LBO by Bain Capital, KKR and Vornado Realty Trust; liquidated in 2018

evidence.description: Bain Capital, KKR and Vornado took Toys R Us private in a 2005 $6.6B leveraged buyout, loading it with ~$5B of debt that cost ~$400M/year to service. The company filed for Chapter 11 in Sept 2017 and liquidated in 2018 — closing ~800 stores and cutting 33,000 jobs, initially with no severance — even as the PE owners collected ~$464M in fees and interest. Congress publicly confronted Bain and KKR over the collapse.

businesses.platform_company: Once ~3,500 stores; controlled by Eddie Lampert's ESL since the 2005 Kmart–Sears merger, now reduced to a handful under the ESL-controlled Transformco

evidence.description: Sears' post-bankruptcy estate sued Eddie Lampert and ESL alleging they stripped more than $2B of assets from the retailer via self-dealing — including the Lands' End spinoff and the 2015 Seritage sale-leaseback of 200+ Sears stores — moving value beyond creditors' reach as the company slid toward its Oct 2018 bankruptcy. The claims settled for $175M. Sears shrank from ~3,500 stores to a handful.

businesses.platform_company: Casual-dining seafood chain; Golden Gate bought it from Darden in 2014, later sold it on; filed Chapter 11 in May 2024

evidence.description: To help finance its $2.1B 2014 purchase of Red Lobster from Darden, Golden Gate Capital sold the chain's real estate for ~$1.5B in a sale-leaseback — pocketing cash while saddling Red Lobster with rent obligations it couldn't sustain. That debt-and-rent burden was widely cited as a key driver of Red Lobster's May 2024 Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

businesses.platform_company: Footwear/apparel maker (formerly the Jones Group); Sycamore's 2014 LBO; filed for bankruptcy in 2018

evidence.description: Sycamore acquired the Jones Group in a 2014 LBO, renamed it Nine West, and moved its most valuable brands (Stuart Weitzman, Kurt Geiger, Jones Apparel) to Sycamore affiliates for below fair value — beyond creditors' reach — while loading Nine West with debt. Nine West went bankrupt in 2018; in the litigation that followed, a court found the former directors may have breached their fiduciary duty by failing to evaluate whether the LBO would render the company insolvent — a landmark warning about PE buyout structures.

businesses.platform_company: Sporting-goods retailer; Leonard Green's 2006 $1.3B LBO; liquidated ~450 stores in 2016

evidence.description: Leonard Green & Partners bought Sports Authority in a 2006 LBO for ~$1.3B, loading it with debt. After missing a debt payment in early 2016, the retailer filed for Chapter 11 in March 2016 and liquidated all ~450 stores. It is one of several Leonard Green retail bankruptcies, alongside J.Crew and Joann.
